obligation: G1 benchmark (memorization guard) + the critical Phase-B bottleneck
G1_guard_validated: The train-vs-held-out gap MEMORIZATION GUARD fires hard on the SwiGLU operators (gap 0.60 and 1.26): train error 0.18-0.25 (great) but held-out 0.79-1.51 (terrible). This is exactly the fit-set false-win the campaign warns about, and the guard catches it -- satisfying G1's acceptance (harness runs q3 + candidates, emits RD vectors, guard fires on an overfit).
CRITICAL_FINDING: Executable-operator synthesis is DATA-BOUND, not architecture-bound, at the current capture scale. 3413-6827 MLP-input tokens is FAR too few to train 30-60M-parameter operators -- they memorize the training activations and fail held-out. Larger operators (m=8704) overfit MORE. The architecture search (G3-G8) CANNOT succeed until the teacher dataset is much larger and more diverse. G2 (large diverse teacher dataset) is the P0 blocker for the whole Phase-B program.
reframe: G2 must generate teacher (h, F(h)) pairs from a LARGE diverse corpus (thousands of prompts x positions, many task families), not the 6827-token capture. This needs teacher forward passes to capture MLP inputs h at scale; F(h) is then computed from the bf16 weights. Regularization + smaller operators help at the margin but do not substitute for data volume.
next: Build the large teacher dataset (G2) as the P0 gate, THEN run the operator-family search (G3-G8) against it with the held-out guard. The current activation captures are the seed; scale is the blocker.
